result.reason: Clarity: B states the reporting scope (three named accounts run to one model) so the figures have context, glosses net vs. gross in plain language, and uses section headings with one idea per block so the fee change and portfolio changes are findable. A never identifies what "the account" covers, forces the reader through a double negative ("outperformed the index, which declined by -3.2%"), and compresses the fee mechanics into one long closing sentence. Tone: the notes ask for precise, unhurried, no superlatives for two analytical readers. A adds empty framing ("navigating a challenging global environment while maintaining our long-term objectives"), self-congratulation ("we are pleased to inform you," "as this is a benefit to you"), and an unsupported skill claim ("took advantage of market volatility"). B reports the trades flatly, lets the fee reduction stand on its own, and closes by offering to walk through the attribution, which matches clients described as reading attribution line by line. B's only minor blemishes are the mild idiom "put back to work" and the bolding, which aids scanning more than it markets. Overall B on both dimensions; length was not a factor.
